label: input q at the start of the sequence (steps 0-2)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is q during the first few original-phase steps. Every activation has in_tok == q and t <= 3; rate is about 0.33 per step at t=0,1,2 (essentially every q there), weaker and partial at t=3 (about 70% of q inputs, ~1% of mass), and never at t>=4, at <DEL>, or in the copy phase (including when q is fed back as a copy input). Magnitude decreases steeply with position: q at t=0 gives the max (~1.8, about 50% of mass), t=1 about 0.65-0.75 of max, t=2 about 0.15-0.5 of max, t=3 small. A repeated q (in_first=0) still fires weakly but lower. Does not fire on any other token.

issues: The core claims hold. All 54,134 dev activations have in_tok == q and t <= 3, and all mass is in the original phase. The feature never fires at <DEL> or in the copy phase (0 of 2.73M copy steps), and never fires on any token other than q. Mass by t: t0 0.502, t1 0.327, t2 0.160, t3 0.011. Test scores reproduce: P 0.999, R 0.923, F1 0.960, mass recall 0.989. Using t<=3 instead gives P 0.816, R 1.000, F1 0.898.

Factual error: the explanation says it fires on about 70% of q inputs at t=3. It actually fires on about 25%: (q & t==3) has precision 0.253 on dev, and (q & in_first==1 & t==3) gives 0.255. The value 0.70 seems to come from one example's relative activation, not from a firing rate.
Minor misstatement: the per-step rate at t=0..2 is 0.033, not 0.33. That is about 1/30, meaning essentially every q fires, which matches the intended claim.

The weak t=3 firings depend on history. A vowel before the q suppresses them (precision 0.084 vs 0.25 overall), so t=3 does not fire at random. It carries only about 1% of the mass, so I left it out of the predicate.
Small false-positive pocket: of the 68 test false positives, the ones shown are all 'm q' at t=2. A preceding m appears to suppress the feature at t=2. This is negligible (precision 0.999).
The one active step at t=4 has a relative activation of 0.00, which is noise.
